rename_teach.M2.S2.T2.C2: The diagonals of a rectangle are equal

questions.name: Carpenter's Problem: length of the other strip
questions.q_figure: Two thin wooden strips crossed over each other like an X, with a thread passed round their four endpoints to make a four-sided frame, one strip marked 8 cm and the other marked with a question mark.
questions.s_figure: Rectangle ABCD with both diagonals AC and BD marked 8 cm and crossing at O, and the triangles ADC and DAB shaded in two colours with AD as their common side.

questions.name: Rectangle Diagonals: equal diagonals crossing at 60°
questions.q_figure: Two equal line segments AC and BD crossing at their midpoint O with the angle AOB marked 60°, and the four endpoints joined in order A, B, C, D to make a four-sided figure.
questions.s_figure: The same figure with the four angles at O marked 60°, 120°, 60° and 120°, the base angles of the triangles marked 60° and 30°, and a right angle marked at each corner of ABCD.

questions.name: Rectangles and Squares, Q2
questions.s_figure: The 30° case drawn: AC of 8 cm with its midpoint O, a second line through O at 30° to AC with B and D each 4 cm from O on opposite sides, and A, B, C, D joined in order to make a rectangle.
Two equal sticks AB and CD crossed at their midpoints O, with a thread passed from A through C to B so that ACBD is a rectangle and the corner at C is marked as a right angle.

questions.name: Four Right Angles: show AD = CB and DC = BA
questions.q_figure: A quadrilateral ABCD with a right angle marked at each of its four corners.
questions.s_figure: The same quadrilateral with the diagonal BD drawn, the angles ∠1 = ∠ABD and ∠2 = ∠CDB marked, and the triangles BAD and DCB shaded in two colours with BD as their common side.

questions.name: Rectangle: show AB is parallel to DC
questions.q_figure: A rectangle ABCD with a right angle marked at each of its four corners.
questions.s_figure: The rectangle with AD drawn as a transversal across AB and DC and the two interior angles ∠A and ∠D marked 90° each on the same side.

questions.name: Rectangles and Squares, Q1
questions.q_figure: Two rectangles side by side: (i) rectangle ABCD with both diagonals drawn and the angle ∠CAB marked 30°; (ii) rectangle PQRS with both diagonals meeting at O and the angle ∠QOR marked 110°.
questions.s_figure: The same two rectangles with every angle at the corners and at O marked: 30°, 60°, 60°, 30° and 120° and 60° at O in (i); 110°, 70°, 35° and 55° in (ii).
A slanted parallelogram with its opposite sides marked parallel and equal and its angles marked 60°, 120°, 60° and 120°.

questions.q_figure: Rectangle PAIR with P at the top left, A at the top right, I at the bottom right and R at the bottom left, and a tilted rectangle RODS sharing the corner R, with O on the side AI, D to the right of I and S below R; PR = 5 cm, RS = 5 cm and the angle ORI marked 30°.
questions.s_figure: The same figure with the right angle at I and the angle ∠ROI = 60° marked in triangle ROI, the right angle ∠ROD marked, and ∠IOD marked 30°.

questions.name: Special Rectangle: which figures are squares
questions.q_figure: Four quadrilaterals in a row, each with a right angle at all four corners: 5 cm by 2 cm, 6 cm by 3.6 cm, 5 cm by 1 cm and 4 cm by 4 cm, labelled (i) to (iv).
questions.s_figure: The same four figures with all four marked as rectangles and only the 4 cm by 4 cm one also marked as a square.

questions.name: Square Diagonals: construct with a diagonal of 8 cm
questions.s_figure: Square ABCD with its diagonals AC and BD of 8 cm drawn crossing at right angles at O, with OA = OB = OC = OD = 4 cm marked.

questions.name: Square Diagonals: angles at a corner
questions.q_figure: A square ABCD with the diagonal AC drawn.
questions.s_figure: Square ABCD with the diagonal AC drawn, the right angle at D marked, and ∠DAC and ∠DCA each marked 45°.

questions.name: Rectangles and Squares, Q3
questions.s_figure: A circle with centre O and two perpendicular diameters PL and AM, with the figure APML drawn by joining A, P, M and L in order and its four equal sides marked.
Square ACBD drawn from the diagonal AB of 6 cm: the perpendicular bisector of AB through its midpoint O with C and D each 3 cm from O, and the arcs used to draw it.

questions.q_figure: Square CASE with C at the top left, A at the top right, S at the bottom right and E at the bottom left, with the midpoints U, V, W and X of its sides joined in order (figure a), next to a second square (figure b) with a tilted square inside it whose four corners lie on the sides of the outer square.
questions.s_figure: Square CASE with the inner square UVWX, the 45° angles of the four corner triangles marked and the right angle of UVWX marked, and a tilted inner square whose corners are at equal distances from the corners of the outer square.

questions.name: Quadrilateral Angles: find the fourth angle
Kites and Trapeziums, Q10
questions.q_figure: A quadrilateral ABCD with a corner that caves in: B at the top, A and C at the bottom left and right, and D a point above the line AC between them, with the angles at A, B and C and the reflex angle at D marked.
questions.s_figure: The same figure with the line BD drawn, splitting it into triangles ABD and CBD.

questions.name: Parallelograms: construct with 4 cm, 5 cm and 30°
questions.s_figure: Parallelogram ABCD with AB = 4 cm, AD = 5 cm and ∠A = 30° marked, with the line through D parallel to AB and the line through B parallel to AD meeting at C.

questions.name: Parallelograms: remaining angles when ∠A = 30°
questions.q_figure: A parallelogram ABCD with the angle at A marked 30°.
questions.s_figure: The same parallelogram with ∠A = 30°, ∠B = 150°, ∠C = 30° and ∠D = 150° marked.

questions.name: Parallelograms: remaining sides of the 4 cm by 5 cm one
questions.q_figure: A parallelogram ABCD with AB = 4 cm and AD = 5 cm marked.
questions.s_figure: The same parallelogram with the diagonal BD drawn, making triangles ABD and CDB, and the sides marked CD = 4 cm and CB = 5 cm.

questions.name: Kites and Trapeziums, Q9
questions.s_figure: A quadrilateral ABCD with AB = CD and BC = AD marked by tick marks, the diagonal BD drawn, and the pairs of alternate angles on it marked.

questions.name: Parallelograms and Rhombuses, Q2
questions.s_figure: Parallelogram ABCD with its diagonals AC = 7 cm and BD = 5 cm crossing at O at an angle of 140°, O marked as the midpoint of each diagonal.

questions.name: Rhombus: construct with a 50° angle
questions.s_figure: Quadrilateral ABCD with all four sides equal and ∠A = 50° marked, with the arcs from B and D crossing at C.

questions.name: Rhombus: remaining angles when ∠A = 50°
questions.q_figure: A rhombus ABCD with the angle at A marked 50°.
questions.s_figure: The rhombus with the diagonal BD drawn, the four angles it makes marked 65° each, and the corners marked 50°, 130°, 50° and 130°.

questions.name: Parallelograms and Rhombuses, Q1
questions.q_figure: Four figures: (i) parallelogram PEAR with parallel sides marked and ∠P = 40°; (ii) parallelogram PQRS with ∠P = 110°; (iii) rhombus UVWX with the diagonal XV drawn and ∠XVU = 30°; (iv) rhombus OIEA with the diagonal OE drawn and ∠OEA = 20°.
questions.s_figure: The same four figures with every remaining angle marked.
Rhombus ABCD with its diagonals AC = 5 cm and BD = 4 cm crossing at right angles at their midpoint O.

questions.name: Geoboard: two perpendicular rubber bands
questions.q_figure: A geoboard (a square board of dots) with two equal rubber bands laid across each other at right angles at their midpoints, making a plus sign.
questions.s_figure: The geoboard with the four ends joined to make a square, and again with one band extended by 2 cm at each end so that the ends make a rhombus.

questions.name: Joining Triangles: sides 8 cm, 8 cm and 6 cm
questions.q_figure: Two identical triangles with sides 8 cm, 8 cm and 6 cm drawn side by side.
questions.s_figure: The ways of joining the two triangles: a rhombus along the 6 cm side, a parallelogram along an 8 cm side with one copy turned half round, and a kite along an 8 cm side with one copy flipped over.

questions.name: Joining Triangles: sides 6 cm, 9 cm and 12 cm
questions.q_figure: Two identical triangles with sides 6 cm, 9 cm and 12 cm drawn side by side.
questions.s_figure: The six ways of joining the two triangles along their 6 cm, 9 cm and 12 cm sides, three giving parallelograms and three giving kites.

questions.name: Kites and Trapeziums, Q1
questions.s_figure: Quadrilateral ABCD made of two equilateral triangles of side 4 cm joined along the diagonal BD, with every side marked 4 cm and the angles marked 60°, 120°, 60° and 120°.

questions.name: Kite: properties of the diagonal BD
questions.q_figure: A kite ABCD with AB = BC and CD = DA marked by tick marks, and its diagonals AC and BD meeting at O.
questions.s_figure: The same kite with the triangles AOB and COB shaded in two colours with BO as their common side, and the right angles at O marked.

questions.name: Kites and Trapeziums, Q2
questions.s_figure: Kite ABCD with the diagonal AC = 6 cm and the diagonal BD = 8 cm, BD being the perpendicular bisector of AC and crossing it at O, with OB = 2 cm and OD = 6 cm marked.

questions.name: Kites and Trapeziums, Q3
questions.q_figure: Two trapeziums side by side: (i) one with its parallel sides horizontal and the angles 135° and 105° marked at the two ends of the longer lower side; (ii) a tilted one with its parallel sides marked with arrows, its two slanting sides marked with equal tick marks, and one angle of 100° marked.
questions.s_figure: The same two trapeziums with every angle marked: 135°, 105°, 45° and 75° in (i); 100°, 80°, 80° and 100° in (ii).
